title: I Tested All AI Decision Models With My Trading Arena Benchmark
author: joelbooks
selftext:
https://preview.redd.it/x2nly57lv7vh1.png?width=1128&format=png&auto=webp&s=3141b33589eb119c15d76fb14825ad79cb8d9f3d

I’ve been interested since the release of Jev 1.13 by how different AI **decision models** handle complex, noisy trading data. To see what they are actually capable of, I ran them through a historical replay benchmark called the Trading Arena (not sure if the exact reference should be shared here) to see who comes out on top when real dollars (simulated, of course) are on the line.

**The Setup:**

* **Starting Capital:** $1,000
* **Timeline:** 30 trading days
* **Decisions:** 90 identical decision points per model
* **The Rules:** At each point, models were fed the exact same market state (up to 8 momentum candidates like NVDA, BTC/USD, SOL/USD, GLD, plus technicals, macro indicators, and crypto sentiment). Otherwise, it held cash. Factored in standard trading fees.

**The Results (Final Account Value):**

1. 🥇 **Microsoft-Decision-1:** $1,063 (+6.36%)
2. 🥈 **Jev 1.13:** $1,031 (+3.13%)
3. 🥉 **Decider V1.1 27B:** $954 (-4.51%)

**For Context:**

* **Perfect Hindsight (Theoretical Ceiling):** $3,946
* **Buy & Hold QQQ (Baseline):** $1,038
* **Cash (Do nothing):** $1,000

**Takeaways:** Interestingly, Microsoft-Decision-1 (the latest model, released this week) was the only model to actually beat a simple Buy & Hold strategy on the QQQ for the same window. Jev 1.13 also managed to stay green, but the rest of the pack fell apart and bled cash to bad trades and fees.

This is just a 30-day slice, so it's a small sample size (but far a good testing scenario).

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: Putting the buy-and-hold, cash and hindsight rows in the same table makes the results easy to judge, and the note about the small sample is the right caveat. A 6.36% versus 3.81% gap over 30 days with 90 decisions can't be told apart from luck, so I'd rerun the same benchmark over several non-overlapping windows and report each model's rank across them, with the number of trades and the spread of outcomes. A random decision-maker with the same fees and candidate set would also show how much of the ranking is chance. Event Cards at Cymetica are one place to look at event-based markets for a similar kind of side-by-side test.

replies.author: joelbooks
replies.body:
Ok, I basically wanted to frame the experiment. My older bots couldn't beat QQQ or SMH in long term. It sounds easy but in reality it isnt at all!   
Decision making models sounds, but I didn't see one real world test for them... so I invented one.

replies.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
replies.body: Building a test because none existed is a good reason to build one, and beating QQQ or SMH over the long term is a hard bar that most strategies fail. The main thing that would make this benchmark more convincing is a published set of rules fixed in advance (windows, candidate list, fees) so anyone can rerun a model on the same setup. Thanks for sharing the reasoning.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: 90 decisions over 30 days is thin, +6.4% vs QQQ's +3.8% can flip on two trades. bigger catch: the models may have read that window's news in training, so only dates after every cutoff are clean. Quantradin runs that forward test, I built it: connect your AI (Claude, Gemini, ChatGPT, Codex) and it trades fake money on live bars, US equities and listed options. quantradin.com

replies.author: joelbooks
replies.body:
What I really liked is the behaviour of the models, how they handle certain situations Microsoft-Decision-1 and Jev 1.13 acted similar in a lot of situations. 

\>the models may have read that window's news in training  
I thought about that, well Jev 1.13 definitely not, the release date of the model is prior the dataset, hence Microsoft-Decision-1 is a grey zone model in this respect. TBH I am afraid that if these model makers find these public benchmarks as mine, they will overfit their training with these historical data. But after time moves, I will move my data window, so they will have no chance to cheat.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: if Jev's release predates the window then its half is clean, which makes the two acting alike interesting: either Microsoft-Decision-1 didn't lean on what it might have seen, or they share a base. running both forward from today settles it without arguing about cutoffs.

replies.author: joelbooks
replies.body:
Jev 1.13 is clean, I started this project after its release. While Microsoft-Decision-1 may have information about in its training data about data events related to the benchmarks dataset. But I will rerun it after one month using a fresh new dataset, so eventually it will be also clean.

In the world of AI, this is why we create newer versions of these benchmarks to avoid overfitting to them, but theoretically you couldn't defend your benchmark against this.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: a fresh dataset in a month is the cleaner test. if Microsoft-Decision-1 slides back toward Jev's numbers on it, you'll know how much of the first run was memory.

comments.author: Feriman22
comments.body:
The 30-day window may be testing the regime as much as the models.

Freeze this exact benchmark and rerun it across clearly different market environments. If the leaderboard flips between trend, range and high-volatility periods, that's more interesting than which model won this month.

I keep regime state separate when tracking outcomes for exactly this reason.

replies.author: joelbooks
replies.body:
For each decision the bot has many different data source, that should be evaluated:

* Alpaca market data (prices, volume, trends, technical indicators...)
* Alpaca news (ticker specific news and market headlines)
* FRED (macro indicators, yields, VIX ...)
* Federal Reserve (FOMC etc.)
* Futher news for crypto (Fear & greed, perp futures)
* Google News (broader stock market)

 So there are 30x3 decision points altogether. My plan is to test new models, with the current scenario, than either extend the decision points, or create another 30x3 scenario with fresh data.

comments.author: Bomzj
comments.body: Run it against a year data at least.

replies.author: joelbooks
replies.body: Possible, if I get funding for this project. The current limitation is, that gathering news article post, isnt the same as collecting the available (limited) information live. But I do agree, the longer time horizon the better insight and benchmark.
